title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 74
paragraphs: The Lydians had arms very closely resembling those of the Greeks. The Lydians were in older times called Maeonians, and they were renamed after Lydus son of Atys, exchanging their earlier name. The Mysians wore native helmets on their heads, carried small shields, and used javelins hardened at the tip by fire. They are settlers from the Lydians, and from Mount Olympus they take the name Olympieni. The commander of the Lydians and Mysians was Artaphernes son of Artaphernes, the same man who invaded Marathon together with Datis.
